title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
author: Dan Goodin
body: Unknown hackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit nodes and reconfigured them to favor unencrypted email traffic and redirect SSH connections through servers they controlled, a researcher reported Tuesday. The hijacking began in late August, when according to Tor volunteers , the attacker used a valid password that had been reused to gain access to a Tor management server. The attacker then installed Ebury , a backdoor written for Linux that was discovered 12 years ago. Mysteries remain Then the attacker connected from the management server to a second Tor server, called Switzerland2, through SSH, using an RSA key that, for unknown reasons, investigators couldn’t find among Switzerland2’s authorized keys. With administrative control of Switzerland2, the attackers installed Ebury there as well. Finally, the attacker reconfigured settings on two exit nodes that Switzerland2 hosted. title: UN says we're going to blow past 1.5º warming, offers a "now what?" answer
author: John Timmer
body: In 2015, all but two countries agreed to make an effort to keep global temperatures from reaching 1.5° C above pre-industrial readings. Since then, most of the world has largely treated what they signed on to as aspirational, and one of the largest emitters (the US) has alternately withdrawn and recommitted to the agreement. Meanwhile, the planet has responded as expected to steadily rising carbon emissions and appears to be practically at the 1.5° limit. On Wednesday, for the first time, the United Nations Environmental Programme (UNEP) acknowledged that reality , and conceded that the goal of keeping warming below 1.5° was no longer a viable one. Instead, its new goalposts focus on keeping both how long we exceed that limit and how much we exceed it by, at a minimum. Doing that will require both dramatic emissions cuts now and the removal of hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere before the century is out. Bowing to the inevitable Depending on which baseline you use to establish pre-industrial temperatures, as well as which reconstruction of global temperatures you rely on, the world has either gotten very close to, or already exceeded the 1.5° milestone. The current El Niño event, which appears exceptionally strong, will almost certainly mean that we've gone over it no matter which records you choose. Read full article Comments

title: Klara and the Sun review: Jenna Ortega fans, respectfully look away
body: Klara and the Sun is a disaster of a movie, though on paper it was promising. The film's source material is Kazuo Ishiguro's popular sci-fi novel . Its content taps into the emerging conversation around artificial intelligence , as the titular Klara is an Artificial Friend, designed to be the perfect companion for a lonely teen. In the lead role is rising star Jenna Ortega, who aims to show range from her hardened Scream character and devotedly monotone Wednesday by playing a smiley robot who's scorned for being "too empathetic." Joining her are celebrated actresses like Amy Adams and Natasha Lyonne. And at the helm is Taika Waititi, who previously adapted Barry Crump's book Wild Pork and Watercress into the beloved coming-of-age action comedy Hunt for the Wilderpeople. However, it's been 10 years since Waititi gifted audiences with the winsome and weird tale of "bad egg" Ricky Baker. Want more film and TV news and reviews delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable s Top Stories newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today. Since then, Waititi earned mixed reviews for Jojo Rabbit, his adaptation of Christine Leunens' Caging Skies in which he cast himself as Adolf Hitler. title: Panel urges NASA to fetch Apollo 15 poop bags and hardware from moon
body: Astronauts should return to the Apollo 15 landing site on the moon and haul home some of its half-century-old poop and hardware, a panel told NASA on Wednesday. A crew would land just north of the site at Mons Hadley far enough away to avoid damaging it. From there, the astronauts would walk over to inspect the rover, lander base, instruments, and power systems the prior crew left behind in 1971. That equipment has endured decades of space radiation and repeated heating and cooling as lunar days give way to nights. Scientists on Earth could study how the lunar environment impacts the hardware over time. A close look at the urine and feces in a lab could reveal how biological material changes and whether it affects the area around it. That "would be foundational information [for] how we need to engineer the systems for lunar bases," said Dan Dumbacher, co-chairperson of the committee, "for anything humans take to the surface of the moon." The mission proposal came from a National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine committee, whom NASA asked to recommend future moon-landing sites away from the lunar south pole, where the agency already intends to build a long-term moon base . In a new report , members of the committee selected four non-polar sites Bhabha Crater, Mons Hadley, Orientale Basin , and Aristarchus Plateau where they believe Artemis astronauts should collect samples, make observations, and conduct experiments. They prioritized locations they believed would benefit from human explorers over uncrewed robots. SEE ALSO: A telescope's survey got interrupted

title: Airbnb hosts can’t make guests do chores under new rules

But now, Airbnb is putting limits on that routine. For reservations booked on or after Nov. 20, hosts generally won t be allowed to ask guests to do the housework any longer. SEE ALSO: Airbnb adds a bunch of new features for travellers What can Airbnb hosts still ask guests to do? The update, announced by Airbnb on Oct. 20 , draws a distinction between light tidying and cleaning the rental for its next occupants. Here's how the company breaks it down: Dishes: Hosts can ask you to leave used dishes in the sink, but shouldn't ask you to wash and put them away. Laundry: Gathering used towels is allowed. Stripping beds or starting a load of laundry generally isn't. Trash: Hosts can ask you to separate garbage and recycling into designated indoor bins, but shouldn't ask you to haul it off-site. Air conditioning: Hosts shouldn't tell you to avoid an amenity advertised in the listing, though they can ask you to turn it off when you leave. title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Tesla published its third-quarter 2026 financial results this afternoon. Earlier in October, it reported its sales and deliveries for the three-month period, selling fewer cars than in the same quarter in 2025 , yet it still beat analyst projections. Now we can see how those sales translate to the bottom line. Tesla brought in $28 billion in revenue in Q3, almost the same as in 2025. Automotive revenues were $20.6 billion, a 3 percent decrease year over year. Perhaps more troubling is the decline in revenue from solar panels and storage batteries—this line of business had been growing, but for Q3 revenue fell 16 percent year over year to $2.9 billion. Services and other revenues, though, which include parts and Supercharger use, grew by a third to $4.6 billion. But the company—like the rest of us—has seen its expenses go up. Operating expenses rose by 39 percent to $4.8 billion, dropping the company’s operating margin to just 2.6 percent; in Q3 2025, Tesla’s margin was 5.8 percent. Net profit fell to $787 million, down 43 percent year over year. What’s more, capital expenditures were up by 110 percent to $4.7 billion, and free cash flow was down 62 percent to $1.5 billion. title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in user privacy case
body: Meta , which has fought numerous youth safety lawsuits this year , now faces a $25 billion penalty for violating New Mexico's consumer protection laws. The order, made Wednesday by a New Mexico judge, is the latest development in a lawsuit filed against Meta by the state in 2021. The case stemmed from the 2018 Cambridge Analytica scandal , in which the U.K.-based data firm employed by Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign exploited Facebook features to harvest and misappropriate the personal data of more than 50 million users. SEE ALSO: Meta: We're sorry for banning No Kings Instagram account New Mexico's lawsuit argued that Facebook generally misled consumers about its data privacy practices, as well as its efforts to moderate misinformation and hate speech. Last month, a New Mexico jury found Meta liable for nearly 44 million violations of the state's consumer protection statute. The jury found that Facebook's unfair and deceptive practices extended to messaging shared by its executives, including Meta's CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Facebook's then-chief operating officer Sheryl Sandberg. "Facebook continued making public representations concerning users' control of data, third-party data misuse, misinformation, hate speech, and equal enforcement after employees, researchers, and senior personnel had internally identified that Facebook could not make good on its public promises," Judge Francis J. Mathew wrote in his decision . Meta said the decision and penalty make it "all but impossible" to do business in New Mexico, according to a statement obtained by Yahoo! Finance .

title: OpenAI's latest AI models are coming to Google Cloud and Antigravity
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Google would certainly prefer that everyone used its Gemini models with Google Cloud services, but soon, you'll have more options. OpenAI and Google have come to an arrangement that will see the former's frontier models arrive in Google Cloud services. Perhaps more importantly, GPT models will soon appear in Antigravity, Google's agent-powered coding tool. For enterprise customers and AI enthusiasts, OpenAI's latest model will appear in Google's "Model Garden" in the coming weeks, adding to its 200-plus options. The garden already offers access to Google's Gemini models, as well as an assortment of open models like Mistral, Llama, and Gemma. Anthropic's Claude AI has also been available for some time. Google says it's now the only large cloud provider offering access to all three leading closed LLMs. While OpenAI notes that Microsoft continues to be its primary cloud partner, the full suite of current GPT 6 and 6.1 models—Astra, Sol, and Luna—will launch on Google Cloud. Astra will naturally cost the most to run, but Google's system supports dynamically moving workloads between LLMs based on performance, latency, and efficiency. Read full article Comments

title: PHP vulnerability: Which websites and services are affected?
body: If some of your usual websites aren t working today, their operators may have temporarily shut them down to keep hackers out. Two serious security flaws have been discovered in PHP , a programming language that helps websites run. On vulnerable servers, those flaws could allow hackers to run their own commands or access sensitive information. Because PHP is used across so many different websites, the same security problem has left operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems. A fix became available on Oct. 21 , but releasing it doesn t automatically secure every affected site. Website operators and hosting providers still need to install the update on their servers. Some have taken sites offline or restricted features while they do that work, creating disruptions for visitors along the way. SEE ALSO: PHP vulnerability: PHP security issues today explained From gaming services to government websites Those precautions have disrupted everything from online forums to gaming services. 4chan switched to read-only mode while awaiting a PHP security update, while Wikimedia , the organization behind Wikipedia, took supporting tools offline until they could be safely patched. In a statement to Mashable, the Wikimedia Foundation confirmed its recent downtime was related to the PHP security issues . title: How O’Neil Thomas turned his love of performing into a creator career
body: Before O'Neil Thomas had millions of followers, he had a third-grade Christmas production and a serious case of stage fright. But the nerves didn t last past curtain call. Watching family members, faculty, and staff stand and applaud, he knew he wanted to keep performing. "I felt something really warm in my heart," Thomas tells Mashable. "I was like, 'I think this is something I want to do for the rest of my life.'" By high school, he was studying performing arts, writing scripts, and filming YouTube sketches between classes and auditions. And as new platforms arrived, he kept finding new places to perform, learning what audiences responded to and how his comedy could work differently on each app. Over the past decade, Thomas, 29, has grown his audience to more than six million across social media platforms , with fans following his social commentary, comedy sketches like his YouTube series Shady Family and viral recreations, including his take on Beyonc 's Grammy-award-winning album Cowboy Carter 's cover art (which earned a shoutout from her team). But his latest project brings that work back to the passion that started it all: acting. His vertical "microdrama" , the 7:33 minute Investigator, Investigator , was selected for New York's inaugural Alza Film Festival, held Oct. 16 18, where he also joined a conversation aptly titled "What Does Creator Even Mean" to discuss the increasingly blurred lines between creators, filmmakers, actors, and producers, especially as the vertical series boom is getting bigger. body: OpenAI says its AI models helped uncover the critical PHP security flaws that have websites across the internet scrambling. In its own Wednesday blog post, the PHP foundation thanked OpenAI , among other industry partners and cybersecurity researchers. The newly exposed flaws could allow attackers to take over servers running PHP, the programming language behind a large share of the web. OpenAI called the bugs one of the most impactful security problems in recent memory. SEE ALSO: PHP vulnerability: PHP security issues today explained According to OpenAI, security firm Calif found one of the critical flaws using the company s GPT-5.6 Sol model as part of Patch the Planet, an OpenAI security program. Security company Wiz also discovered and reported both vulnerabilities on its own, OpenAI said. PHP s maintainers led the work on the fixes. OpenAI, Wiz, Cloudflare, and other partners contributed research and helped prepare protections before the flaws went public. OpenAI President Greg Brockman added more detail in a post on X . title: Delivery robots scan faces and collect customer biometric data, lawsuit alleges
body: Two Chicago men are suing delivery robot companies Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics for allegedly collecting their biometric information without consent. The two separate class action lawsuits were filed earlier this month. Both claim that the robots' external cameras and internal LiDAR technology are used to scan and collect measurements of customers' faces and hands as they approach the devices. That data was then retained and used to train AI systems, according to the plaintiffs, and attached to personally identifiable information like names and addresses. SEE ALSO: Judge asked to toss 60-year prison sentence over use of Flock cameras One suit filed against Coco Robotics claims the company didn't disclose to customers that its device would scan and collect information, thereby violating Illinois privacy laws. It also extends the privacy violation claim to the use of remote human operators, who were allegedly able to watch the delivery and scanning in real-time. The two cases similarly hinge on the fact that neither customer chose to use delivery robots will ordering food, but were instead assigned to robots by the company after placing their orders. Their data was then sold to third parties, including OpenAI, the plaintiffs claim. The lawsuits cite company disclosures indicating that video and sensor data can be licensed for AI training . Both Serve Robotics and Coco Robotics provide robotic delivery services for popular food delivery platforms, including DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub. title: Judge rejects Trump’s wild claim EPA can dismiss data center pollution lawsuits
author: Ashley Belanger
body: Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI is stuck facing a lawsuit over alleged data center pollution after Donald Trump failed to convince a judge that his Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has complete control over all Clean Air Act lawsuits and can dismiss any suit at whim. Soon after unpermitted gas turbines were discovered powering Musk’s giant Colossus data center in Memphis, Tennessee, the NAACP sued . Its lawsuit sought an injunction requiring xAI (which, following a merger , is known now as SpaceXAI) to use the best available pollution control technology when operating the turbines and ordering penalties up to $124,426 per day per violation. Without such remedies, the turbines risked drastically spiking pollution in already vulnerable neighborhoods housing predominantly Black communities nearby, the NAACP argued. To block the lawsuit, Trump tried to intervene, arguing that the EPA had the power to unilaterally dismiss lawsuits any time the president decides against enforcing the Clean Air Act. According to Trump, it would supposedly “not serve the public interest” if citizens were allowed to seek massive civil penalties to punish polluting AI firms that were trying to get data centers operational as fast as possible to support Trump’s AI Action Plan . body: Smart TVs running operating systems from Samsung, Vizio, and Roku continue sending data to automatic content recognition (ACR) endpoints after users opt out of tracking in the devices’ settings, according to research published on Monday. The paper from Northeastern University researchers points to potential privacy violations from some of the biggest TV brands. ACR captures video screenshots or audio clips from smart TVs and sends the data to remote servers, where it's used for things like measuring content viewership and serving targeted ads. The paper, "Watching the Watchers: Privacy Analysis of US Smart TV Automatic Content Recognition," examined eight smart TV OSes across 12 smart TVs from 10 manufacturers (Amazon, Hisense, LG, Roku, Samsung, Sony, Supersonic, TCL, Vizio, and Westinghouse) to examine when smart TVs use ACR and how effective opting out of user tracking is. title: PHP vulnerability: PHP security issues today explained
body: The team behind PHP released emergency security updates on Wednesday to fix two critical vulnerabilities, a day after details about the flaws leaked online. The UK s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is urging organizations to install the fix immediately. What is PHP? PHP is a programming language that runs on web servers. When you load a webpage, PHP often runs behind the scenes, retrieving data from databases and building the page before it reaches your browser. BleepingComputer notes that it powers many websites, including content management systems, online stores, and custom web services. According to the NCSC , PHP is also built into a range of other products. The NCSC says the two flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, could allow an attacker to run their own commands on a PHP-based server without logging in. This is called remote code execution, and it s one of the most serious kinds of security bugs. According to the NCSC, an attacker could overload PHP s memory to corrupt it, then, under certain conditions, use that corruption to take control of the server. One of the flaws involves how PHP processes form submissions and file uploads. PHP rated each flaw 9.2 out of 10 on CVSS, the industry s standard severity scale. Security firm watchTowr described them as a perfect 10, BleepingComputer reported, and so did an anonymous Hacker News post that has since been deleted. Researchers have started calling the bugs "PHP2SHELL." The fixes were originally planned for a coordinated release later this week, so companies would have time to prepare. Then, inf

title: Android 17 QPR3 Beta 2: Everything new, everything fixed
body: There's a new Android beta out there for your perusal. Google has released the second beta for the third quarterly platform release of Android 17, available for installation on Pixel devices now. You can install it now by enrolling your device in Google's beta program. Sometimes, these betas come packed with lots of exciting new toys to play with, on top of various bug fixes. This is not necessarily one of those times. SEE ALSO: iPhone vs. Android on privacy-invasive bloatware: Which lets users remove pre-installed apps? According to Google's release notes , as well as some reporting by 9to5Google , there are a couple of small new features and a bunch of fixes in this update. One new feature is the ability to require a phone unlock in order to change quick settings like Bluetooth, WiFi, and airplane mode. Normally, you can do that from the lock screen. There are also new themes, custom icons, and weather effects for your phone's wallpaper to play around with. As for the rest of the update, it sounds like it's mostly unexciting (but probably necessary) bug fixes. Google fixed an issue that caused phones to crash and reboot during normal use, as well as another one that caused devices to shut down unexpectedly during WhatsApp video calls. Apparently, paired smartwatches were also seeing an issue where they would continue ringing even after a phone call was answered. That has been fixed, among other smaller issues. title: Samsung’s 5K monitor has good gaming chops and a great price
body: There are quite a few 5K monitors out there. Many of them are designed to appeal to Mac users who are looking for cheaper Studio Display alternatives without giving up the pixel-dense 218ppi screen. However, if you’re interested in hearing about one with gaming chops, Samsung’s 27-inch Odyssey G80HF seems like one of the best monitors out there to satisfy your niche, but respectable desires. Currently, you can grab this model for $599.99 at Amazon and B H Photo , which beats its best price by $100. Samsung 27-inch Odyssey G8 5K monitor Where to Buy: $949.99 $599.99 at Amazon $949.99 $599.9 at B H Photo The G80HF supports two display modes with its Fast IPS panel: 5K at up to 180Hz refresh rate, or 1440p with up to a 360Hz refresh rate. Samsung touts Nvidia G-Sync compatibility as well as AMD FreeSync Premium to ensure the monitor’s refresh rate remains in lockstep with your GPU’s frame rate output. The monitor features a DisplayPort 2.1 port (just one, and Samsung doesn’t advertise its bandwidth), two HDMI 2.1 ports, and a USB hub for charging or connecting two USB-A 3.2 Gen 1 accessories. As a gamer, one of my favorite features here is the one-millisecond response time. That’s a very common spec among gaming monitors — even in ones that cost hundreds less — but it’s a bit of a rare spec in a 5K monitor at this price. I tested KTC’s sub-$500 model last year , and gaming on it was a pretty atrocious experience despite having what it claimed to be gaming-ready capabilities. For $200 more ($799.99), LG’s 27-inch UltraGear evo 5K Mini LED monitor delivers slightly better specs.

title: Apple iPhone Duo review: This changes everything
body: Apple's iPhone Duo is an important phone. The iPhone has been around for two decades, and this is the first time Apple has tried something completely different with its best-selling product. Other companies have had foldable phones for years, but none of those carry the weight of a foldable iPhone. Apple s ecosystem of iPhone-related products, services, apps, and accessories is vast, and this is a massive new entry in that book. After a week with the iPhone Duo, I m happy to report that Apple has done an amazing job. The iPhone Duo is the most exciting iPhone since the first one. It s not just an iPhone that turns into a small iPad when you unfold it. The form factor and the clever things Apple has done to the user interface open up new possibilities, and after a few days, I found myself doing stuff on the iPhone Duo that I don t typically do on a regular iPhone: I ve played games for hours at a time, I ve tied apps together in a side-by-side view that enhanced my productivity; I ve used the Duo as a secondary display, next to the MacBook on my desk. It s not all perfect. There are drawbacks, compromises, and there are bugs to iron out. title: Apple iPhone Duo vs. iPhone 18 Pro: First-hand impressions, how to decide
body: Planning to upgrade your iPhone this year? If you want the most feature-packed device, the choice is usually easy: You'd buy the latest iPhone Pro Max, and this time around, that's the very impressive iPhone 18 Pro Max . So, should you go with the iPhone 18 Pro Max or the iPhone Duo ? Each is powerful in its own right, as they both have Apple's new Apple Silicon chip A20 Pro. But both are missing important features that the other has. Our first-hand experience: iPhone Duo vs. iPhone 18 Pro Max Credit: Stan Schroeder/Mashable Mashable has now had plenty of hands-on time with both devices. Here's what we can say based on our real-world testing: If you want the most powerful iPhone on the market, get the iPhone 18 Pro Max. If you want a whole new iPhone experience, get the iPhone Duo. As Mashable's Stan Schroeder wrote in his iPhone Duo review , the new foldable is "the most interesting iPhone since the first one." Apple has successfully pulled off its first foldable device, despite a few minor quirks. The user experience is excellent, and Apple really thought through all the ways a larger, foldable screen can benefit iOS. title: Review: Carrie is a triumphant remix with one major flaw
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Carrie White, the telekinetic prom queen from hell, is one of the most beloved horror icons in popular culture. First introduced in Stephen King's 1974 novel, Carrie , the character was immortalized in director Brian De Palma's 1976 adaptation, widely regarded as one of the best horror films of all time. It's certainly one of the best King adaptations. So Mike Flanagan faced a massive challenge when he signed on to create an eight-episode miniseries for Prime Video based on the book, released just in time to mark the 50th anniversary of de Palma's film. I was among the skeptics who questioned why a Carrie miniseries was even necessary, although as a diehard Flanagan fan ("Flana-fan"?), I was willing to give him the benefit of the doubt. If anyone has an affinity for smartly adapting horror in general, and King's work in particular, it's Flanagan. And you know what? With one (very big) exception, Flanagan pulls it off, giving us a richly textured version of the story that is as much about kindness and lost innocence as bloody, vengeful rage—although we get plenty of the latter, too. (Many spoilers below for the novel and the 1976 film , but there are no major reveals for the new series until after the second gallery. We'll give you a heads-up when we get there.) title: The past, present, and future share a show floor at Pinball Expo 2026
author: Nick Indge
body: It's October in the Midwest, which means it's time for the pinball world to descend on a convention center in Chicagoland for the annual Pinball Expo. Once thought to be an entertainment sector slowly bleeding out, pinball has come back in a big way in recent years. I visited one of Chicago's last old-school manufacturers before heading down the road to see what's new in the silver-ball universe. Behind the silver ball Hundreds gathered on a brisk fall Friday morning outside Stern Pinball's headquarters in Elk Grove, Illinois, waiting to enter a Wonka-like wonder factory where piles of raw parts become licensed creations from Jaws to the brand-new Fallout . Stern invited me to tour its offices and factory floor before heading off to the convention in nearby Schaumburg, Illinois. An early-morning line begins to form outside of Stern HQ as buses of Pinball Expo attendees arrive for tours. As I stood with my tour group in Stern Pinball's HQ lobby, mouth agape at the dozens of machines lining the walls, we were greeted by the man himself, Gary Stern, who gave us some background on the company's 40-year history. After a stop at Gary's podium, we were ushered to the factory floor entrance, where Stern employee and legendary game designer George Gomez briefed us on the tour rules and answered questions. According to Gomez, "at any given time, Stern controls 90 percent of the current pinball market, and everybody else splits the rest." Read full article Comments

title: Fantasy readers are leveling up. Welcome to LitRPG.
body: You couldn't walk very far at New York Comic Con this year without running into Dungeon Crawler Carl . The bestselling fantasy series was everywhere on the convention floor, from merch booths to an author signing with Matt Dinniman. Even I couldn't resist picking up a Princess Donut sticker. And while the premise of a man and his ex-girlfriend's cat fighting their way through an apocalyptic, video game-inspired dungeon created by aliens might sound absurd, its popularity points to something much bigger happening in the world of books . Welcome to LitRPG, a genre that combines the immersive storytelling of fantasy with the mechanics of role-playing games. Characters level up, earn experience points, and unlock new abilities, much like they would in World of Warcraft or Dungeons Dragons . It's a genre that's been thriving in online communities for years, but now it's having a mainstream moment, thanks in part to the runaway success of Dungeon Crawler Carl . According to The Atlantic , the first eight volumes of the series have sold more than 17 million copies , with a TV adaptation currently in development for Peacock. SEE ALSO: Comic conventions are becoming content studios. NYCC is embracing the shift. And the publishing industry is taking notice. After years of building audiences through self-publishing and online fiction platforms, LitRPG titles are now finding their way onto bookstore shelves . title: Regretting buying a Kindle with ads? Heres how to remove them.
body: Buying a Kindle with lockscreen ads is a hotly debated topic on the Mashable shopping team. To be clear, none of us are pro-ad, but we are pro-saving money. Kindles without lockscreen ads cost $20 more than those with ads, and these days, we're all looking to save money where we can. But if you buy a Kindle e-reader with lockscreen ads, you're not stuck with them. Perhaps you just bought a Kindle, or maybe you've had one for years; either way, it's not too late to free yourself from the lockscreen of capitalism. Unfortunately, it will mean spending $20, but it's a worthy investment. How to remove lockscreen ads from your Kindle Total Time 5 min What You Need Computer Internet browser Kindle Step 1: Go to 'Manage Your Devices' Log into your Amazon acc﻿ount and under the 'Account' tab, navigate to the device tab and pick your device. Credit: Amazon / Mashable Step 2: Select your device After you find your device listing, click on it and find the special offers section. title: What is brain stacking? TikToks latest trend wants you to put down your phone
body: TikTok has a new suggestion for anyone worried that endless scrolling has turned their brain into mush: Pick up a book. Or a crossword puzzle. Or a Sudoku. Better yet, stack them all together. It's called "brain stacking," and the idea is pretty simple. Instead of reaching for your phone whenever you have a spare moment, you keep a collection of books, puzzles, journals, and other mentally stimulating activities within arm's reach. Think of it as a little library of things to do when you're bored that don't involve staring at another screen. And in an era when " brain rot " has become part of our everyday vocabulary, it's not hard to understand the appeal. What is brain stacking? Brain stacking is exactly what it sounds like: assembling a stack of activities designed to engage your brain. On TikTok and Instagram Reels, creators are showing off their collections of Sudoku books, crossword puzzles, novels, journals, and other analog activities, often as part of their morning or nighttime routines. The goal isn't necessarily to become smarter overnight. It's to replace some of the time you'd otherwise spend doomscrolling or bloomscrolling with activities that require a little more concentration, creativity, or critical thinking. In one TikTok, highlighted by Essence 's Girls United , creator @shykikii shares her nighttime brain-stacking routine , which includes journaling, Sudoku, and reading before bed. She credits fellow creator and "brain stack queen" @mandyrulez for the inspiration and for seemingly coining the term. Some creators are also incorporating timed brain stacks

title: A telescopes survey got interrupted by a comet nobody knew existed
body: A European spacecraft built to map galaxies has discovered a new comet serendipitously, proving it can do more than study dark matter and dark energy in the distant universe. The Euclid Space Telescope spotted the space snowball, dubbed C/2026 S1 (Euclid) between Sept. 16 and 24, after the renegade had smudged five image sets. The European Space Agency's mission, launched in 2023, takes long exposures of faraway galaxies, not high-speed photography of zippy objects in our own solar system. But moving-object software, developed by Mikko P ntinen, a doctoral student at the University of Helsinki, flagged an errant streak. Finding and removing stray signals is crucial for the mission to photograph about one-third of the entire sky in every direction around Earth. "By predicting [the object's] position, I could identify it in other images," P ntinen said in a statement . "Further inspection revealed that it had a fuzzy cloud around it, indicative of an active object like a comet that is shedding dust and gas." The results show Euclid, a mission in partnership with NASA , can find new comets early, while they are still fairly far from the sun . That buys astronomers time to watch it activate and change as it approaches, as well as study what it's made of. Tracking a comet over time allows researchers to get a more accurate depiction of its orbit, which tells them how close it will come and how bright it might get. title: Cops raid office of RFK Jr. allies planning “unethical” vaccine trial on babies
author: Beth Mole
body: Police in Guinea-Bissau raided the offices of Danish researchers on Monday, seizing doses of hepatitis B vaccine intended for a vaccine trial for newborns. International health experts have called the trial " unethical ," but anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has attempted to fund it with US taxpayer dollars. Under Kennedy, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced in December that it had awarded the Danish researchers—led by married couple Peter Aaby and Christine Stabell Benn of Bandim Health Project— an unsolicited $1.6 million grant to run the trial . Aaby and Stabell Benn are controversial vaccine researchers who claim vaccines cause overlooked harms. They have been repeatedly praised by Kennedy, but are currently under investigation for alleged scientific misconduct by Danish authorities. Plans for the trial were halted in January as widespread condemnation erupted over the trial's design, which would potentially expose thousands of newborns in the country to hepatitis B, risking a lifelong infection that can lead to liver cirrhosis, cancer, and premature death. Outrage flared again after a Rolling Stone story earlier this month claimed the CDC set aside another $1.6 million in funding in late September and planned to move forward with the trial. title: Microsoft reportedly projects $1,200 to $1,800 price for 2028 Project Helix
author: Kyle Orland
body: We haven't heard many details about Microsoft's upcoming "Project Helix" gaming hardware since the company announced it in March as a device that will "play your Xbox and PC games." In a new wide-ranging profile of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma , though, Fortune alludes to a dual release strategy for upcoming Microsoft gaming hardware, with "a next-generation handheld device" planned by the end of next year and a 2028 holiday season console release that could cost between $1,200 and $1,800. That future console price range is based on what has "internally been projected" at the company, according to Fortune. But the price for consumers could come down if "Microsoft decides to subsidize the cost," the outlet says, as many console makers have done in the past . While a $1,200 starting price would be historically high for the game console market, even accounting for inflation , it also reflects a new normal: The slowdown in Moore's Law and AI-driven component shortages mean cutting-edge gaming hardware just isn't as cheap as it used to be. This year, the Steam Machine broke the $1,000 starting price , while the 2-year-old technology in the PlayStation 5 Pro is now going for $900 , and the 6-year-old Xbox Series X now starts at $750 . title: Gemini's Personal Intelligence is coming to cars
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Google kicked off 2026 with the addition of Personal Intelligence to Gemini, allowing its AI to pull in more of your data to formulate answers. It started as a paid feature but eventually came to all Gemini users. However, this feature wasn't available in the car until now. Google is rolling out Personal Intelligence to Android Auto and Google Built-in, and it is still, thankfully, an optional feature. As Google points out , a generative AI's outputs are better "when it knows the world and knows you," which is correct in an uncomfortable sort of way. The more context you can provide to a model, the better the output will be at the end of the token shuffle. Since Google has so much of your data already, it sees Personal Intelligence as a differentiator versus other AI systems. You don't have to provide the AI context because it already has it from apps like Gmail and Calendar. Personal Intelligence is beginning its rollout in Android Auto today, and it will come to vehicles with Google built-in in the next few months. As an aside, "Google built-in" is questionable branding, but it refers to cars that run Google software in the infotainment system rather than projecting an interface from your phone. Very few vehicles have Google built-in, but Google often releases new car features on them first. This time, it's the other way around. Read full article Comments

title: OpenBSD 8.0 arrives with security record still intact
author: Nick Indge
body: OpenBSD 8.0 is here, marking the project's 61st release and continuing its schedule of semiannual releases dating back to 1996. What started more than 30 years ago as a fork of NetBSD has grown into one of the most security-conscious operating systems in active development. In a post to the project's announcements mailing list, OpenBSD founder Theo de Raadt highlights a host of improvements included with the latest version and writes that the project remains "proud of OpenBSD's record of more than thirty years with only two remote holes in the default install." The latest OpenBSD version brings new features and improvements across the board. These changes, particularly the new Intel Arc support and expanded virtual address space, should improve compatibility with modern graphics cards and allow the system to map more than 4GB of VRAM . Some of the major updates noted in the release newsletter are as follows: Added support for Intel Arc A-Series (DG2/Alchemist) graphics cards. 512GB kernel virtual address space on AMD64, up from 4GB, allowing VRAM mapping above 4GB. Added hibernation support for ARM64 systems. A new RPKI -to-router daemon: rtrd(8) . RISC-V improvements including kernel support for the 'V' vector extension and support for Advanced Interrupt Architecture. Wireless network driver additions and improvements, including 802.11n and 40 MHz channels for the qwx(4) wireless driver . Added support for up to 64 virtual CPUs per guest virtual machine. title: The Internet goes on high alert after discovery of 8 compromised TLS certs
author: Dan Goodin
body: Security personnel around the world are on high alert Tuesday following the discovery of eight TLS certificates with private keys so weak they could allow anyone to mint trusted browser and app credentials for any site on the Internet. As of late morning Tuesday, browser makers and some major apps and programming languages had blocked all eight of the intermediate certificates. There are no reports of certificate transparency logs, which track the issuance of all browser-trusted certificates, showing the compromised keys being used maliciously. The threat remains far from over, however, because it will be hard and time-consuming to update other key parts of the Internet, such as Linux distributions and embedded and Internet of Things devices. One word: bonkers The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based certificate authority eMudhra Limited. An informal advisory published to emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com over on Tuesday posted the message “We have a problem here - Wayne.” The words were digitally signed using the private key of one of the eMudhra certificates. With proof that the reporting party had control of the key, defenders scrambled because the same key could be used to sign unauthorized certificates that would be trusted by millions of servers worldwide. title: Does anyone actually want to win the medium-lift race in the United States?
author: Eric Berger
body: It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation. The initial 100-series variant of the Antares rocket was kind of a hot mess. The rocket used old Soviet engines built during the era when Apollo astronauts were landing on the Moon. Decades later, in the 1990s, Aerojet acquired the engines and refurbished them for a rocket that would launch in the 2010s. Predictably, on the fifth launch of an Antares rocket in 2014, it exploded. The Antares vehicle is the last of a dying breed of medium-lift rockets—defined as having a lift capacity of 2 to 20 metric tons—in the United States. Nearly a decade and a half later there is a new generation of medium-lift vehicles coming online, and they are starkly different from Antares, which had not just Russian engines but a core stage manufactured in Ukraine. title: Quantum error correction goes well beyond breakeven
author: John Timmer
body: Running complicated algorithms on quantum computing hardware is going to require the use of logical qubits, where collections of hardware qubits are linked together in ways that allow errors to be detected and corrected. In general, the more hardware qubits you dedicate to each logical qubit, the better the chances are of identifying errors. But, given that the hardware qubits are prone to errors, adding more of them also increases the probability that errors will occur. If the hardware error rate is too high, then growing the logical qubit will only make matters worse. Fortunately, several companies have demonstrated hardware where the error rate is not too high. Several demonstrations show logical qubits are beyond the breakeven point, where adding more qubits improves performance. The problem is that the improvement isn't very dramatic. To lower error rates to levels we'll need to run complex algorithms, we'd have to add a completely impractical number of qubits to each logical qubit. On Monday, Quantinuum announced that its current generation of hardware is capable of scaling well beyond the breakeven point. Each step up in the size of logical qubits improved some measures of their performance by a factor of over 10. Read full article Comments

title: Meta tries to scapegoat staff who downloaded torrents to spare execs
author: Ashley Belanger
body: In copyright lawsuits over AI training, Meta has spent weeks blaming staff for downloading torrents. The company has now been ordered to name executives who authorized decisions to pirate books from shadow libraries like Anna’s Archive and LibGen, TorrentFreak reported . In a discovery order impacting a class action raised by book authors—including Richard Kadrey and Sarah Silverman—as well as a lawsuit from publisher Entrepreneur Media, Magistrate Judge Thomas Hixon largely agreed that Meta must clearly identify key decision-makers. Following testimony from Meta staff who downloaded torrents, the order could expose a wider range of supervisors, managers, and executives whom staffers said greenlit the piracy. Meta had been hoping to avoid detailing the chain of command, particularly for leadership involved in early AI training. According to a Meta court filing , its initial efforts to compile massive AI datasets were managed through an “informal approach" where supposedly nobody with authority made any decisions. title: Having Windows Outlook access problems? An update might have caused it.
body: Microsoft may have borked Outlook for some folks with a new Windows update. Specifically, a Windows Server security update has caused access issues for Outlook on some Exchange Server systems, according to a Microsoft security note (cited by BleepingComputer ). This is specifically affecting systems running Windows Server 2019 and later, per Microsoft. As a result, users may not be able to access Outlook, or sent messages might just remain in the Outlook outbox without actually going anywhere. SEE ALSO: Microsoft president warns AI is less regulated than milk and washing machines There is no firm fix for this problem just yet. Microsoft says that the severity of the problem will differ from server to server, with some not encountering any problems at all. In a different post , Microsoft urged users not to uninstall the problematic update, instead offering a workaround: Open an elevated Command Prompt on an Exchange Server Enter the following as a command: "reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Rpc" /v EpmapSavedContextCap /t REG_DWORD /d 65536 /f" Reboot the server That should help alleviate the issue until Microsoft offers a long-term fix for it. title: Polestar tries to quantify what it’s like to drive a performance car
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: The human desire to go fast is old, dating back at least as far as the first time some adventurous Yamnaya saw a horse on the Pontic-Caspian steppe and thought, “I bet if I jumped on that thing’s back, it would be faster than walking.” A thousand years later, someone else invented the wheel—and the chariot—and humanity was ready to roll. Now, about five millennia since that first horseback ride, equestrianism is mostly a leisure activity, and we drive cars, propelled by motors with more power than an entire herd of beasts could muster. Acceleration, top speed, and lap times are the usual ways we quantify that performance, and performance electric vehicles are currently in an arms race to see which one can hit 60 mph in the least amount of time. But measuring a car’s performance is easy—all you need is a stopwatch and a track. How about measuring the effect of car performance on the driver? title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on October 20, 2026
body: The Moon is more than half illuminated, which means we're getting closer to the Full Moon. Each night the Moon will appear bigger in the sky, with lots of opportunity to spot some features on its surface. What is today's Moon phase? As of Tuesday, Oct. 20, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 65% of its surface visible. Tonight, you should be able to spot the Mare Crisium, the Tycho Crater, and Mare Fecunditatis without any visual aids. If you have binoculars you'll also see the Endymion Crater, the Alphonsus Crater, and the Appenine Mountains. Plus, if you have a telescope, you'll also see the Apollo 15 and 16 landing spots, plus the Rima Hyginus. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on October 25 or 26, depending on your timezone. What are Moon phases? The Moon takes around 29.5 days to travel around Earth, and its appearance changes throughout the month. As it moves around our planet, we see different amounts of its sunlit side, from a slim crescent to the quarter phases and eventually a Full Moon. It then begins the cycle again. As NASA explains, these phases are caused by the Moon's changing position relative to Earth and the Sun. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. title: Final Fantasy Resonance doesnt hit as hard as the classics, but its still a fun throwback
body: My first exposure to a certain type of Final Fantasy fan occurred in 2006, when a friend of mine angrily insisted that a game can't be Final Fantasy if it doesn't have turn-based combat. This was in response to the hybrid real-time combat of Final Fantasy XII , and series developer Square Enix has been forsaking that kind of guy in the two decades since. There hasn't been a traditionally turn-based mainline Final Fantasy in 25 years, which makes Final Fantasy Resonance exciting. A new title assembled using assets from the mobile title Brave Exvius , Resonance follows in the footsteps of last year's Octopath Traveler 0 in turning a phone game into a console experience that will live after its predecessor's servers are inevitably shut down. Resonance is not as large or audacious as Octopath was, and its main story relies a bit too much on tropes and concepts from previous Final Fantasy stories to stand on its own. Thanks to pleasurable combat that's wonderfully easy to bust wide open and a solid sense of exploration, this throwback RPG was worth the 40 or so hours it took me to finish. SEE ALSO: 'Zelda: Ocarina of Time' is my favorite video game ever. After playing the remake, I get the vision. Final Fantasy Resonance is full of ideas you've heard before The best Final Fantasy games have some of the most emotionally affecting and thought-provoking stories you'll find in any big-budget RPG. I often put Final Fantasy X , in particular, on a pedestal thanks to its compelling combination of gut-wrenching romance and an examination of how theocracy can take hold over a society. Al

title: Antigravity A1 unveils Watch Remote for 360-degree drone
body: Drone company Antigravity has launched new wrist- and finger-mounted remote controls for the Antigravity A1, allowing users to fly the 360-degree video drone without a headset . These more subtle control options mean users can now capture some very impressive selfie footage without goggles getting in the way. SEE ALSO: Review: Is the Antigravity A1 drone the DJI replacement we've been hoping for? Introduced in December last year, the Antigravity A1 aims to offer high-quality 360-degree video while still being easy for amateurs to pilot. At the time, the A1 could only be flown using Antigravity's Vision goggles and Grip controller, both of which came bundled with the drone. However, while this control scheme offered an immersive and intuitive experience, the Vision goggles prevented drone pilots from seeing what was around them. This limited A1 users' situational awareness, meaning they needed a spotter to watch both the drone and its pilot when flying. The FAA requires recreational pilots to maintain visual line of sight with their drone, or else have an observer watching who is in direct communication with them. Credit: Antigravity The Antigravity A1 Follow Me Bundle has now addressed such limitations with its Watch and Ring Remotes, new control options that allow users to use their drone without the Vision goggles. This means Antigravity A1 users can film themselves without their faces obscured as well as fly it solo, making the drone much more versatile. title: The 6 best character cameos in Final Fantasy Resonance
body: Sometimes it's fun to see an old homie you haven't seen in a while. Final Fantasy Resonance understands that, to great effect. The new throwback-style RPG from Square Enix remixes assets from the mobile game Brave Exvius into a single-player console and PC adventure, complete with turn-based combat inspired by the classics. "Visions," ghostly apparitions of characters from previous Final Fantasy games, are a big part of the combat, with each one imbuing their associated main party member with new powers and powerful special moves that can turn the tide of any fight. With that in mind, I wanted to take a few minutes to talk about my six favorite visions in Final Fantasy Resonance . Some are here just because I think they're cool, and others because of their role in combat. Let's get into it. title: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
author: Dan Goodin
body: Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through Web links, researchers reported Monday. Like many online services, Muse allows users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed. A single query is all that's required Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. But a central design decision for constructing URLs has made the links easy to discover. As a result, researchers from security firm Claroc said they were able to enumerate 6,800 links Muse users created for sharing conversations with others. title: Japan launches mission to bring home a piece of the Martian moon Phobos
author: Stephen Clark
body: Japan launched a $578 million mission Monday on a five-year expedition to land on the largest moon of Mars and retrieve samples for return to Earth, a daring international project that could yield new insights into the formation of the Solar System. The robotic Martian Moons eXploration mission, known as MMX, lifted off at 3:41 pm EDT Monday (4:41 am Japan Standard Time Tuesday) from Tanegashima Space Center in southern Japan. The MMX spacecraft rode into orbit atop a 207-foot-tall (63-meter) H3 rocket, Japan's flagship launch vehicle. The rocket assigned to MMX debuted a new souped-up configuration with four strap-on solid rocket boosters, full-throttle main engines, and an extended payload shroud to accommodate the demands of Japan's heaviest and most ambitious interplanetary mission to date. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess.
